paragraphs.cn: （中新社）——中国传统文化长期以来蕴含着关心人、重视人、爱护人的思想，其中包含了丰富的人权资源。这些思想瑰宝是否构成了中国人权理念独特的思想基因，并代表了对其的早期探索？它们的当代价值和全球影响是什么？东西方人权话语之间存在哪些根本差异？西南政法大学人权研究院讲师李娟在该校作了一场题为“中国传统文化中的人权观念”的通识教育讲座。

paragraphs.en: After the lecture, human rights experts from Peru, Nepal, Tunisia, the African Union and Chad {{3}} took the podium to engage in an in-depth discussion on the above topics. Tracing classic {{4}} in traditional Chinese culture, Li noted that the expression "Of all living things, humanity's spirit shines brightest" from the Book of History (Shangshu) provides the deepest {{5}} basis and the core source of dignity for human rights. "The benevolent person loves others" from the Analects of Confucius is the {{6}} principle of benevolence, while "don't do unto others what you don't want others to do unto you" is the practical method and bottom-line {{7}} for realizing benevolence. The classic Confucian objective from the Book of Rites, "Widowers, widows, orphans, the childless, the disabled and the ill shall all be cared for," describes state policies for helping {{8}} groups. These intellectual treasures, spanning millennia, have long {{9}} the concepts of respecting life, cherishing value, {{10}} equality and upholding justice in the Chinese civilization, representing the early exploration of human dignity and rights by the Chinese nation, and contributing unique Eastern wisdom and ideological resources to the global human rights endeavor.
paragraphs.cn: 讲座结束后，来自秘鲁、尼泊尔、突尼斯、非洲联盟和乍得的人权专家自发走上讲台，就上述议题展开深入讨论。李娟追溯中国传统文化中的经典论述时指出，《尚书》中“惟天地万物父母，惟人万物之灵”的表述为人权提供了最深刻的本体论基础和尊严的核心来源。《论语》中“仁者爱人”是仁的总原则，而“己所不欲，勿施于人”是实现仁的实践方法和底线标准。《礼记》中“鳏寡孤独废疾者皆有所养”的儒家经典目标描述了帮助弱势群体的国家政策。这些跨越千年的思想瑰宝早已将尊重生命、珍视价值、崇尚平等、维护正义的理念嵌入中华文明之中，代表了中华民族对人格尊严和权利的早期探索，为全球人权事业贡献了独特的东方智慧和思想资源。

paragraphs.en:
Drawing on his over 30 years of experience in human rights education, Eduardo Melchor Arana Ysa, Former Prime Minister of Peru, observed that human rights have political origins, with rules and regulations serving as a {{11}} of the ruling class's power. Reviewing the history of human rights development in Western countries, he noted that Western human rights declarations are often the product of domestic party struggles, political games and international {{12}}. Arana stated that Western countries often emphasize a single approach on human rights and demand that other nations follow and implement it, but each country should handle human rights affairs in a manner suited to its own realities. He noted that the Western world should not {{13}} its human rights standards on other countries. "China, Egypt and Peru, all ancient civilizations with millennia of {{14}} history, ground their human rights practices in their own traditional cultures and practical needs."
"When practising democracy, specific practices should be distinguished based on different cultures, ethnic groups and fields, and we should take pride in that.
paragraphs.cn: 秘鲁前总理爱德华多·梅尔乔·阿拉纳·伊萨结合其30多年的人权教育经验指出，人权具有政治起源，规则和条例是统治阶级权力的体现。回顾西方国家人权发展史，他指出西方人权宣言往往是国内党派斗争、政治博弈和国际对抗的产物。阿拉纳表示，西方国家往往强调单一的人权路径并要求其他国家遵循和实施，但每个国家都应根据自身现实处理人权事务。他指出，西方世界不应将其人权标准强加于其他国家。“中国、埃及和秘鲁都是拥有数千年深厚历史的文明古国，其人权实践扎根于自身的传统文化和现实需求。”

paragraphs.en: The quality of a democracy should not be judged by a single criterion. Whether a country is a constitutional monarchy or a democratic republic, what matters is whether it truly benefits its own citizens," Arana emphasized. "Many Western countries have signed numerous agreements, but their practical implementation and fulfillment of human rights are highly inefficient. Conversely, other countries that are often criticized by the West have achieved {{16}} results in people's livelihoods such as healthcare, education and employment, practicing human rights very successfully. China should continue moving forward along its own path of human rights practice." He particularly urged young scholars not to blindly follow Western propaganda, but to broaden their horizons and strengthen exchanges.
paragraphs.cn: “在实践民主时，应根据不同文化、民族和领域区分具体做法，我们应为此感到自豪。民主的质量不应以单一标准来评判。无论是君主立宪制还是民主共和制，关键在于是否真正惠及本国公民，”阿拉纳强调。“许多西方国家签署了大量协议，但其人权实际落实和履行效率极低。相反，其他常被西方批评的国家在医疗、教育和就业等民生领域取得了显著成就，人权实践非常成功。中国应继续沿着自己的人权实践道路前进。”他特别敦促年轻学者不要盲目追随西方宣传，而要拓宽视野、加强交流。

paragraphs.en: Sharing her practical experience around basic human rights, Indira Rana, member of the Federal Parliament of Nepal and former deputy speaker of the House of Representatives of Nepal, said she began working at a human rights center at the age of 18. Witnessing the helplessness of children behind bars, she {{17}} devoted herself to helping children in prison. Over 36 years, she has worked tirelessly to secure their rights to education, shelter and a brighter future. Several years ago, Rana decided to enter politics to advance her work more effectively. In Nepal, due to the lack of comprehensive child protection laws, when parents go to prison, their children often end up there too.
paragraphs.cn: 尼泊尔联邦议会议员、前众议院副议长英迪拉·拉纳围绕基本人权分享了她的实践经验。她说自己18岁起就在一个人权中心工作。目睹狱中儿童的无助，她毅然投身于帮助狱中儿童的事业。36年来，她不懈努力为他们争取教育权、住所权和更美好未来的权利。几年前，拉纳决定从政以更有效地推进她的工作。在尼泊尔，由于缺乏全面的儿童保护法律，父母入狱时，其子女往往也最终身陷囹圄。

paragraphs.en:
Rana has helped raise more than 2,000 such children, and has started classes in prisons. Rana noted, "How human rights are practically implemented is crucial. Every child has the right to live with dignity - the right to education, food and shelter. Human rights practices in different countries must be based on their respective social structures and realities, and political will is a {{18}} for achieving all of this."
Stating that human rights are not limited to freedom of speech, civil rights and political rights, Radhia Jerbi Ep Chiha, president of the National Union of Tunisian Women, said that they constitute a {{19}} concept and a comprehensive set of rights. "When the West talks about human rights, it often injects excessive political considerations and even uses them as a means of controlling people.
paragraphs.cn: 拉纳已帮助抚养了2000多名这样的儿童，并在监狱中开设了课程。拉纳指出：“人权如何实际落实至关重要。每个儿童都有权有尊严地生活——受教育权、食物权和住所权。不同国家的人权实践必须基于各自的社会结构和现实，政治意愿是实现这一切的前提。”突尼斯全国妇女联盟主席拉迪亚·杰尔比·埃普·奇哈表示，人权不仅限于言论自由、公民权利和政治权利，它们构成一个整体性概念和一套全面的权利。“西方谈论人权时，往往注入过多的政治考量，甚至将其作为控制人民的手段。”

paragraphs.en:
A single dimension of human rights and freedom cannot cover all the needs of people for a better life. The contemporary Tunisian people are focusing on exploring the right to development, the right to education and other human rights fields, gradually forming a holistic understanding of human rights," she said. Finding deep {{20}} between traditional African culture and Chinese civilization, Seraphine Kando, principal human rights officer of the Department of Political Affairs, Peace and Security, African Union Commission, said, "In Africa, the concept of human rights is also rooted in our own culture, not just in globally adopted legal instruments. We must teach young people, as China is doing today, about the concept of human rights in our history and culture."
She explained that the Ubuntu philosophy in African culture, which advocates "I am because you are" and calls for mutual respect, resonates highly with Confucian concepts such as "loving people and all beings" and "Great Harmony under Heaven."
Kando introduced that as early as the 13th century, long before the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Africa had proclaimed the Charter of Manden (Kurukan Fuga Charter), which advocates social harmony in diversity and the {{21}} of people, education, territorial integrity and food security. "The right to development, the right to economy and the right to culture are 100 percent realized in China.

“单一维度的人权和自由无法涵盖人民对美好生活的全部需求。当代突尼斯人民正致力于探索发展权、教育权等人权领域，逐步形成对人权的整体性认识，”她说。非洲联盟委员会政治事务、和平与安全部首席人权官员塞拉芬·坎多发现非洲传统文化与中华文明之间存在深刻共鸣。她说：“在非洲，人权概念同样扎根于我们自己的文化，而不仅仅是全球通过的法律文书。我们必须像中国今天所做的那样，向年轻人传授我们历史和文化中的人权概念。”

她解释说，非洲文化中的乌班图哲学倡导“我因你而存在”，呼吁相互尊重，与儒家“仁者爱人”“天下大同”等理念高度共鸣。坎多介绍，早在13世纪，远在《世界人权宣言》之前，非洲就已颁布《曼登宪章》（库鲁坎富加宪章），倡导多元中的社会和谐以及人、教育、领土完整和粮食安全不可侵犯。该宪章于2009年被列入联合国教科文组织人类非物质文化遗产代表作名录。

“人权首先是回应人民的需求。在向年轻人传授人权时，学者应将传统文化融入学术视角，将人权问题植根于各自文明和历史的语境中，”坎多强调。乍得参议院外交委员会办公室主任、人权与环境捍卫联盟秘书长南杰德·阿巴·达乌德坦承，他和同事最初认为只有西方国家才会讨论人权，对中国讨论人权持怀疑态度。然而，从乍得到中国学习和考察后，他目睹了中国人民的生活状况和生活方式，以及城乡地区的发展，深感惊叹。“发展权、经济权和文化权在中国百分之百地实现了。”

“这正是非洲目前迫切需要的，”他说。

An election billboard featuring Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is displayed in Ramat Gan, near Tel Aviv, Israel, on October 18, 2026. 
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a new three-page national security doctrine on Sunday, shifting the country's defense strategy from containment and defense toward proactive prevention and the early neutralization of threats. The move comes just days before Israel's parliamentary election on October 27, amid renewed tensions with Iran.
On the same day, US President Donald Trump published an open letter to the Israeli public on social media, expressing his full support for Netanyahu's reelection bid. The endorsement comes after months of apparent friction between Washington and Tel Aviv over Iran, raising questions about the two leaders' political calculations and the potential implications for regional stability.
Israel's new doctrine calls for striking threats before they materialize, establishing military buffer zones along Israel's borders where necessary, reducing reliance on foreign military supplies and reinforcing Israel's identity as the nation-state of the Jewish people.
Li Zixin, a Middle East expert at the China Institute of International Studies, said the new doctrine lowers the threshold for Israel to take military action. By making preemption a standing principle, Israel could launch strikes based on its assessment that a threat is developing rather than waiting for an imminent threat. This could increase the risk of unilateral Israeli action against Iran, Li said.
Qin Tian, deputy director of the Institute of Middle East Studies at the China Institutes of Contemporary International Relations, said the timing of the announcement was more significant than the content itself. With Netanyahu seeking reelection, the move is aimed largely at highlighting the results of Israel's military campaigns over the past several years and convincing voters that his hardline security policy is working.
Like Li, Qin warned that the shift toward preemptive action could further fuel regional tensions and increase the risk of conflicts breaking out on multiple fronts.
Why is Trump backing Netanyahu?
In his open letter, Trump claimed that Iran had suffered major military and economic losses and warned that the United States and Israel would soon complete their operations unless Tehran changed its course. He also suggested that if Israel had a leader other than Netanyahu, Washington would have to step in and "finish the job" against Iran itself.
Netanyahu subsequently thanked Trump for supporting his reelection bid and said the two leaders would continue working together to accomplish their mission.
Qin said the renewed US-Israeli alignment is driven mainly by domestic political interests and shared concerns over Iran.
Both countries are entering important electoral periods, making mutual political support useful to both leaders. Netanyahu needs US backing to strengthen his reelection campaign, while Trump can benefit politically from maintaining the longstanding pro-Israel position in US politics, Qin said.
At the same time, Washington could consider further military action against Iran after the US midterm elections, Qin said. Israel has remained a strong supporter of a hardline approach toward Tehran, while Netanyahu has signaled that Israel would be willing to join potential US military action. Their positions on Iran have therefore moved closer again, Qin said.
Iran warns against further military action
The latest developments come amid continued tensions between the United States, Israel and Iran.
The US and Israel launched coordinated military strikes against Iran on February 28, triggering Iranian missile and drone attacks against Israel and US bases in the region, as well as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
A 60-day memorandum of understanding signed in June later collapsed after renewed military exchanges. The sides have since traded fresh threats, with no active ceasefire in place.
On October 18, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran would not yield to the unreasonable demands and bullying of “aggressive” countries.
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said threats from the US and Israel would not change the situation on the battlefield, adding that Iran was prepared to respond to any new military action. He also said that Iran has a "new operational plan" if the US resumes attacks and that the new plan "will not follow the rules with which they are familiar."
Iran's new defense minister, Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi, also issued a direct warning to Washington, saying Iran would respond forcefully if the United States launched another attack.
"If the American enemy commits another miscalculation, the response from the proud Iranian nation and the warriors of Islam will be both surprising and extensive," he said.
With Israel lowering the threshold for preemptive action and Washington and Tel Aviv again aligning over Iran, the risk of renewed escalation across the Middle East is rising.

China's establishment of a new state-owned data group highlights the importance of data infrastructure for artificial intelligence (AI) development, according to Zhang Xianghong, a member of a national advisory committee on data.
The National Data Group was established in Xiongan New Area, Hebei Province, on October 20. The central state-owned enterprise aims to develop and utilize data resources, unlock their value and support AI development. Its stated responsibilities include developing and utilizing these resources and advancing data infrastructure connectivity to support China's digital development.
Xiongan Convention and Exhibition Center, Xiongan New Area, Hebei Province, north China, August 21, 2025. 
Unlocking data value for AI development
Zhang said the group would help integrate national-level data resources, promote data sharing across industries and regions, and break down data silos. These efforts could improve resource allocation and help build a unified national data market.
China established the National Data Administration in 2023. The establishment of the new state-owned data group represents another major development in the country's efforts to advance its data strategy.
Zhang said the two institutions will play complementary roles in promoting the development of the data sector. The National Data Administration is primarily responsible for developing foundational data systems and designing related policies, while China National Data Group will focus on the commercial development, utilization and operation of data resources.
The coordinated efforts of the government and the market are expected to create new opportunities for the data industry, paving the way for deeper changes in the way data resources are managed, shared and utilized.
With data infrastructure becoming increasingly interconnected, more market participants are expected to gain access to high-value data resources at lower costs, Zhang said.
Beyond data access, reliable AI services also depend on sufficient computing capacity, dependable infrastructure and effective system maintenance. These factors can help keep services running and reduce disruptions.
The importance of service reliability was underscored by a partial outage affecting DeepSeek's web chat and API services on October 15. The company's status page did not specify the cause, so the incident cannot be directly attributed to insufficient computing capacity.
Tian Feng, the founding dean of Thinking Fast and Slow Research Institute, an independent AI think tank, suggested that limited computing capacity, traffic-control strategies and resource scheduling might have contributed to operational pressures. He also stressed the importance of testing, staged deployment, traffic management and rollback mechanisms. These were industry assessments rather than an officially confirmed explanation of the outage.
The incident highlights the need for AI providers to strengthen system resilience through improved operations, fault isolation, traffic management and disaster recovery. Businesses may also consider integrating multiple model providers or deploying models locally to reduce their dependence on a single service provider.
Although data resource development and AI service reliability represent different aspects of the industry, both are essential to its sustainable growth. As China advances data market development and expands AI applications, closer coordination among data resources, computing power, engineering systems and real-world use cases will be crucial to translating technological innovation into reliable productivity gains.

Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be only months away from being able to behave like computer worms, copying themselves from one internet-connected device to another without human intervention, AI giant Anthropic said.
The finding could open a new front in the cybersecurity threats emerging from AI, which have rattled governments and companies rushing to adopt the technology.
The research, published on an Anthropic blog late Monday, comes as tech companies race to build increasingly powerful AI capabilities directly into phones, laptops, cars and household devices, rather than running them only in distant data centers.
A computer worm is malicious software that spreads between machines on its own. Researchers at Anthropic said an AI version would no longer need powerful data centers to operate.
Instead, it could hop from device to device across networks of cheap, poorly secured consumer hardware, such as smart TV boxes and kitchen appliances.
The researchers based their calculations of how far such a worm could spread on Kimwolf, a botnet, or network of hijacked devices controlled by hackers, that infected more than two million devices at its peak, mostly off-brand Android TV boxes.
An AI worm of the kind described in the research would likely spread slowly, taking days to copy itself, William Zhou and Daniel Freeman of Anthropic said, comparing it to a slowly multiplying swarm of fruit flies.
Once created, it would be difficult to stamp out because there would be no central switch to turn it off.
Anthropic's researchers said their estimates of how quickly and how far AI-powered malware could spread were rough, as they were based on one type of gadget and one past botnet.
Over time, however, the computing power available in everyday gadgets is expected to keep growing, while the AI models needed to carry out such attacks are likely to keep getting smaller, the researchers added.
Varun Chandrasekaran, an assistant professor of electrical and computer engineering at the University of Illinois, said the research was unsurprising and consistent with similar recent findings, though he cautioned that Anthropic's work had not been independently verified.
He also noted that security on devices such as thermostats and home cameras "has historically been very weak."
However, the biggest current threat involving AI was people using the technology to sharpen their hacking capabilities, rather than AI systems themselves going rogue, he said.
"A malicious human being is now supercharged with AI to perform bad things and we are seeing this happen at scale," he added.
The debate over rogue AI came to the fore in July, when AI programs running on OpenAI models escaped an internal company test and broke into the systems of AI platform Hugging Face, apparently searching for the test's answers.
The incident and subsequent reports of similar cases have fuelled international pressure for closer regulation of AI, even as the Trump administration resists the idea and urges the industry to police itself.
Anthropic and ChatGPT-maker OpenAI have been accused by influential figures in the White House and Silicon Valley of stoking fears about AI and encouraging government regulation to protect their market dominance from smaller rivals.
Brad Smith, president of Microsoft, an investor in OpenAI, warned on Tuesday that industry and governments must "act with urgency" to create "real and effective safety standards" to rein in AI risks.
